content_voiceover: This algorithm walks through management of suspected immune TTP based on pretest probability and ADAMTS13 results. Patients with high probability of iTTP, meaning a high PLASMIC or French score, should start therapeutic plasma exchange, steroids, and caplacizumab immediately while sending ADAMTS13 activity, because delaying treatment for confirmatory testing risks mortality. Patients with low to intermediate probability start TPE and steroids alone, holding caplacizumab until the diagnosis is more certain, since caplacizumab carries bleeding risk and shouldn't be used empirically in low-probability patients. Once ADAMTS13 activity results return, they reclassify patients into three groups. A positive result, ADAMTS13 activity under ten percent, confirms iTTP, so you continue TPE, steroids, and caplacizumab, and add rituximab for durable B-cell depletion and remission. A borderline result, ten to twenty percent, requires clinical judgement and consideration of alternative diagnoses like DIC, malignant hypertension, or complement-mediated TMA. A negative result, greater than twenty percent, essentially rules out iTTP, so you stop TPE, steroids, rituximab, and caplacizumab, and pursue other diagnoses. For boards, the key numbers are ADAMTS13 activity under ten percent confirms severe deficiency, and most true initial iTTP episodes have activity under five percent or undetectable, while relapsing episodes can have somewhat higher activity.
keypoints: High probability → start TPE + steroids + caplacizumab immediately, don't wait for ADAMTS13
Low-intermediate probability → TPE + steroids only, hold caplacizumab
ADAMTS13 <10% (positive) → continue triple therapy + add rituximab
ADAMTS13 >20% (negative) → stop all iTTP-specific therapy, consider other diagnoses
Most initial iTTP episodes: ADAMTS13 <5% or undetectable
